key_insight: Ensemble QSP uses a three-layer hierarchical memory system to keep long-horizon multi-agent LLM workflows stable and context-bounded across extended autonomous research tasks.
engineering_relevance: This architecture shows how to scale scientific agent systems for persistent, quantitative modeling by preventing context drift while preserving domain constraints and task continuity.
method: Three-layer hierarchical memory with capped state categories and eviction of completed work.
Five specialist worker agents coordinated by domain-expert principal investigators.
Physics-based checklists and structured-domain knowledge enforce quantitative consistency.
evidence_signal: Across 104 runs, mid-term project state stayed bounded (median 301 tokens, max 4,050), and benchmarking showed autonomous PK/PD model selection, improved PK parameter recovery over single-agent baselines, and stable performance across different LLMs and prompt phrasings.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful PI-agent configuration and domain-specific checklists, so performance may vary when ported to new scientific domains or when those constraints are incomplete.
paper_title: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
